title: Most Consistent Batsman? Variance Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Two batsmen from the NCERT book play ten matches each and both average 53 runs. Batsman A swings from 0 to 117; batsman B stays between 46 and 60. Which one is more consistent, and can one number prove it? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 13, Statistics) we learn the variance and the standard deviation.

You will watch every gap from the mean turn into a real square: the areas add to 32, the average square has area 4 (the variance), and its side is 2 (the standard deviation). Step by step we reach σ² = (1/n)Σ(xᵢ - x̄)², σ = √σ² and the shortcut σ² = (1/n)Σxᵢ² - x̄². A side-by-side of variance (squared units) and standard deviation (back in runs) for both batsmen, a pause-and-think question, a worked example (6, 8, ..., 24: variance 33, SD about 5.74), the exam trap of stopping at the variance, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
